title: Friction-based slot-damping and probabilistic admission smoothing for continuous-batcher
author: Maya R. Singh
description:
Context and motivation: We observed tail-latency spikes under mixed KV-heavy and short-request workloads when continuous-batcher admission reacted too aggressively to transient load spikes. Existing admission heuristics were binary (accept/reject) and used hard timeouts which led to oscillation and short-request starvation. This PR introduces a friction-based slot-damping mechanism plus probabilistic admission smoothing to reduce oscillation, protect short requests, and be aware of KV-pinned state.

What this change does (single-line sections joined as one string): Introduces a per-slot damping coefficient (friction) which slows aggressive slot reallocation when recent dequeue rate is highly variable; implements a lightweight probabilistic admission gate that weights admission chance by a smoothed score (recent latency, slot-utilization, and KV-pin-pressure); adds a KV-pin decay hint that reduces friction for slots servicing requests that are already KV-pinned to avoid unnecessary penalties; plumbs a new scheduler metric family to surface friction, admission_probability, and pinned_slot_ratio. The new algorithm is designed to preserve continuous-batcher throughput while reducing 99th/99.9th percentile tail latency regressions.

Design details and rationale: - Friction coefficient (0.0-1.0) is maintained per-slot and updated with an exponential moving average of relative queue volatility: friction_t+1 = friction_t * (1 - alpha) + alpha * clamp(volatility_score, 0, 1). High volatility raises friction which temporarily reduces cross-slot preemption and slot-stealing. - Probabilistic admission uses a logistic transform to convert smoothed signals into admission_probability = sigmoid(k*(score - offset)). The score aggregates: normalized recent latency, slot utilization ratio, and KV-pin pressure. - KV-pin decay hint: when a request finds its KV cache warm (pin=true), we apply a short decay to friction so the slot can be reused quicker. This prevents long-lived friction from hurting already-warmed work. - Soft-timeout steering: instead of hard-reject at single timeout boundary, the admission gate lowers probability gradually as requests near deadline thresholds (configurable hysteresis windows). - Backwards-compatible config defaults keep previous behavior if feature flags disabled. We added runtime knobs exposed in the scheduler config: enable_friction, friction_alpha, admission_k, admission_offset, kv_pin_decay_ms, soft_timeout_window_ms.

Testing and benchmarks: - Microbenchmarks: synthetic mix (70% short 5-20 token, 30% KV-heavy fetch+generate) run across 3 GPU shapes. Results: 95th latency unchanged, 99th reduced by ~18%, 99.9th reduced by ~32% under the mixed load compared to baseline. - Long run soak: 24h soak with bursty arrival patterns shows steady-state throughput within 2% of baseline and significantly fewer short-request timeouts. - KV regression tests: validated that KV-warmed paths show lower friction and re-use slots. - Added unit tests for friction update rules, admission probability math, and deterministic behavior under seeded RNG for probabilistic admission.

Commits (summary): - Add friction coefficient state and updater (+roundtrip counters) - Implement probabilistic admission gate and soft-timeout steering - Add KV-pin decay hint integration and config - Expose scheduler metrics and console panel hooks - Tests and microbench harness updates - Docs: add scheduler tuning guide and default config rationale

Files changed (high level): - scheduler/continuous_batcher/scheduler.go (core algorithm changes, friction state) - scheduler/continuous_batcher/admission_gate.go (new admission logic) - runtime/kv/kv_cache.go (kv pin hint API extension) - prometheus/metrics_registry.go (new metrics) - docs/ops/scheduler_tuning.md (new tuning guide) - tests/scheduler/friction_test.go (unit tests) - benchmarks/continuous_mixed_workload.yaml (benchmark config)

Small illustrative snippet (in description, single-line code-like): friction = friction*(1-alpha) + alpha*volatility_score; admission_prob = 1/(1+exp(-k*(score-offset)))

Review conversation (high level single string): Reviewer Alex: "Nice approach — probabilistic gate should smooth transitions. Can we prove monotonicity of admission_prob vs score?" Author reply (Maya): "Added unit tests asserting monotonic mapping and edge-case saturation; also added comments with math rationale." Reviewer Diego: "Concerned about adding RNG variance to tail metrics." Author reply: "Admission uses deterministic seeded RNG during tests; in production we use per-worker entropy but aggregated metrics are robust — added CI soak check." Reviewer Priya: "Do we observe any cost increase?" Author: "No meaningful token-cost change; throughput unchanged in long runs." approvals: "Alex Chen approved; Diego Martínez approved; Priya Nair approved after minor doc updates." Merge notes: "Squashed commits, tagged release-candidate. Merged to main. Feature gated off by default; rollout via config opt-in and can be toggled per-cluster for gradual rollout."

CI and rollout: "CI matrix: unit, integration, lint, go vet, e2e soak. One flaky e2e run retried and passed; final CI status: pass. Rollout plan: enable on internal canary pool for 72 hours, monitor friction/admission metrics and tail latency dashboards; if regressions observed, revert via config flag or scale cohort down."

Release notes: "scheduler: Added friction-based slot-damping and probabilistic admission smoothing to the continuous-batcher to reduce tail latency under mixed KV-heavy workloads. Feature is opt-in via scheduler.enable_friction and tunable via scheduler.* knobs."
